boundary_edges.trust_level: All incoming P2P requests must be validated for block number range (>= 15,537,393 for post-PoS). Pre-PoS data requests must be rejected. Message format must be validated against eth/70 protocol spec.
Block number scope validation required. Must reject requests targeting blocks below Paris upgrade boundary. Rate limiting on request volume to prevent resource exhaustion.

Full block header validation required: difficulty must match computed expected difficulty using EIP-649 rules (fake block number with 3M offset for post-Byzantium). Block reward must be exactly 3 ETH (post-Byzantium). Fork activation block numbers must be checked.

EIP-150 gas repricing must be applied for all IO-heavy operations (SLOAD, BALANCE, EXTCODESIZE, CALL, etc.) at post-Tangerine Whistle blocks (>= 2,463,000). Gas costs must accurately reflect computational cost to prevent DoS.

The checkpoint root must be verified against a trusted source (weak subjectivity assumption). The bootstrap object returned must be cryptographically verified against the checkpoint root. No authentication of the provider itself is possible.

All updates must be validated against sync committee signatures. At least 2/3 supermajority of sync committee signatures required. Finalized header advancement must be verified. Fork version transitions must be handled correctly.
Responses from peers must be cryptographically verified. Multiple peers should be queried to prevent eclipse attacks. Connection to at least one honest full node assumed.
Must validate: (1) current_epoch >= CAPELLA_FORK_EPOCH, (2) first valid change per validator index, (3) full process_bls_to_execution_change validation. Reject/ignore messages failing any check.
Fork digest must match expected Capella fork digest. Block contents including embedded bls_to_execution_changes must be fully validated.

Fork version must be correctly determined via compute_fork_version for each block's epoch. Serialization format must match the fork version. Incorrect fork-version mapping could cause deserialization failures or acceptance of malformed data.

Despite authenticated local channel, all signing requests must be checked against slashing protection DB. Block slot must be >= minimum previously signed slot. Attestation source/target epochs must be >= minimums. No surround voting. Missing signing roots treated as conflicts (conservative).

Validator must be completely stopped during import. File must pass JSON schema validation, genesis_validators_root must match current network, all BLS public keys must be valid, signing roots format verified.

Full validation pipeline: JSON schema, genesis root match, BLS key validity, signing root format. Missing signing roots must be treated as potential conflicts (conservative interpretation). Duplicate public keys must be merged safely.
All request arguments must be validated (method field required). Input must be sanitized. Rate limiting enforced. Provider must not contain private data. Provider-Wallet isolation must be maintained.

Explicit user consent required before exposing any account addresses. Consent dialog must be browser-isolated from DApp manipulation. Origin must be accurately displayed. Permission caching must be per-origin.
Full input sanitization, rate limiting, Provider-Wallet isolation. Provider must contain no private user data. All methods requiring authorization must check permission state.

Consent dialog must be isolated from DApp JavaScript. Origin displayed must be accurate (no spoofing). Developer mode must default to disabled. User must understand security implications of granting access.

Third-party iframes blocked by default. First-party iframes require sandbox compatibility check. Third-party access only via explicit Permissions API grant. Sandbox attribute must include allow-same-origin for first-party.
window.isSecureContext must be true. Origin must be potentially trustworthy per W3C Secure Contexts spec (HTTPS, localhost, file://). HTTP non-localhost blocked unless developer mode enabled.

chainId must be verified in hex format. Disconnect events must trigger appropriate error propagation (ProviderRpcError codes 4900/4901). Chain changes must be validated before emitting chainChanged events.

Full transaction validation required: signature verification, nonce checking, gas limit validation, intrinsic gas coverage, sender balance check, blob count limits. Transactions trigger EIP-3651 COINBASE warming, may invoke SHA256 precompile, and may hit INVALID opcode.

Withdrawal list content must be validated: compute withdrawals trie root and verify against header withdrawals_root. Amount conversion from Gwei to Wei must be checked for overflow. Blob gas parameters must match EIP-7691 limits.

Full block validation: withdrawals_root commitment verification, blob count <= MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK_ELECTRA (9), blob gas <= MAX_BLOB_GAS_PER_BLOCK (1,179,648), all transactions valid, state transitions correct.
ForkID must be validated against local chain configuration. Stale peers must be rejected. Incompatible fork configurations must cause disconnection. CRC32 collision resistance assumed sufficient.
Client identity data is self-reported and MUST NOT be used for security-critical decisions. RLP decoding and ASCII validation required. Data may only be used for non-critical analytics.
Full block validation required including InvalidBlock exception handling, transaction validation (nonce, signature, gas, balance), and state integrity checks (no empty accounts in state).

Proof validation pipeline: verify proof_data non-empty, cryptographic proof verification via proof engine, duplicate detection, prover pubkey whitelist check, BLS signature verification using DOMAIN_EXECUTION_PROOF.

Proof content must be validated even from semi-trusted local engine. Proof data should be non-empty, proof_gen_id should be tracked, and the resulting proof must pass independent verification before signing and broadcast.

SCO files must be audited: verification scripts checked for unsafe operations, target block heights must be hardcoded, no unlocked wallets during verification, expected code hashes validated before state changes.

Validator withdrawal requests must be validated by CL: validator index verified, withdrawal address confirmed, amount within expected bounds, monotonically increasing index assigned. Bounded quantity per block enforced.

Must validate: attested slot freshness (exceeds all previously forwarded or matches with supermajority >= 2/3), propagation timing from slot start, BLS aggregate sync committee signature. Stale or invalid updates must be dropped.
Must validate: attested header slot freshness, propagation timing, sync committee BLS signature, consistency with finality data. Invalid updates dropped.
Requested block root must be for a post-Altair finalized block. If data unavailable, respond with ResourceUnavailable error code 3. Must not serve unfinalized or pre-Altair data.
Count bounded by MAX_REQUEST_LIGHT_CLIENT_UPDATES (128). Start period and count must be validated. Only return updates for sync committee periods with available data.

cell_mask must be validated: nil when no type-3 transactions present, valid B_16 bitmap otherwise. Transaction hashes must be validated. Announcements trigger probabilistic role assignment (p=0.15 provider, p=0.85 sampler).

Cell data must be validated per EIP-7594. Noise column (C_extra=1) must be checked: if provider fails to return noise column, flag as misbehavior. Maximum C_req=8 columns per request. At least 2 distinct providers must be observed before sampling.

Full validation pipeline: (1) corresponding new_payload_request previously seen, (2) first proof for (root, type, prover_pubkey) tuple, (3) prover is active validator in current state, (4) valid BLS signature, (5) proof data non-empty and within MAX_PROOF_SIZE, (6) valid message structure.
Response bounded by MAX_EXECUTION_PROOFS_PER_PAYLOAD (4). Block root must reference a known block. Only return locally stored valid proofs.

Full parameter validation required: blockHash format (valid 32-byte hex), mutual exclusivity with fromBlock/toBlock, block existence verification. Must handle non-existent block hashes gracefully with error code -32000.
Must validate block number and uncle index parameters. Must correctly determine EIP-1559 fork status to include/exclude baseFee field. Must handle non-existent uncles gracefully.
Bloom filter search must handle worst-case false positive rates. Query parameters (address, topics) must be validated. Resource limits should prevent unbounded log scanning.

Full block validation required: header validation (sequential numbering, timestamp, gas limit, difficulty, parent hash), ommer validation (max 2, no duplicates, age 1-6, valid ancestry), transaction execution, and root hash verification (state root, tx root, receipt root, logs bloom).

Full transaction validation: ECDSA signature recovery, nonce match, balance >= gas*price + value, sender is EOA, intrinsic gas check, available gas check. SSTORE operations must be correctly metered per EIP-1283 three-value tracking. Refund counter must be capped at 50% of gas consumed.

EOF structural validation required: header parsing, metadata marker (0x05) detection, metadata size range (1-65535), section position ordering (metadata before data). Invalid containers must be rejected. Metadata content is opaque and not validated at protocol level.

Must validate chainId hex format (EIP-695), verify chain exists in wallet registry, confirm wallet can service target chain. Must display requester identity and target chain to user for informed consent. Must mitigate fingerprinting via chain probing. Must cancel pending requests/confirmations on chain switch.

SELFDESTRUCT is deprecated (EIP-6049). Current semantics transfer balance to beneficiary and mark contract for removal. Future breaking changes expected. Implementations must handle current semantics correctly while preparing for deprecation.

Must verify PoW result <= 2^256/difficulty. Difficulty calculation must correctly apply bomb delay (subtract 3M blocks). Block reward must be exactly 3 ETH (Byzantium). Ommer rewards must follow formula ((8 - age) * 3 ETH) / 8.
Must validate proposer index, BLS signature, slot timing. Execution payload validations are replaced with bid-based checks in Gloas fork.
Must verify builder is active via is_active_builder, payment > 0, fee_recipient and gas_limit match proposer preferences, builder can cover bid via can_builder_cover_bid. BLS signature must be valid.
Must verify builder BLS signature, block root matches known block, payload matches bid. KZG commitments relocated to bid message must be correctly validated.
Must verify proposer is assigned to declared slot in next epoch. BLS signature validation required. Preferences must be well-formed with valid fee_recipient, gas_limit, and slot assignment.

Responses must match request parameters (start_slot, count, requested roots). Response size limited to MAX_REQUEST_BLOCKS_DENEB. All received blocks and envelopes must pass structural validation before integration into local database.
Call data bytes are entirely attacker-controlled. buffer_read must correctly zero-pad out-of-bounds reads. Memory expansion gas must be charged before copy.

Blob versioned hashes are provided by the transaction submitter. Index bounds must be checked; out-of-bounds returns zero. blob_versioned_hashes list integrity must be validated during transaction decoding.
Authorization chain_id, signature (y_parity, r, s), and nonce must all be validated. ECDSA signature recovery must be correct. Invalid authorizations must be rejected without side effects.
gasleft must be strictly greater than 2300 for SSTORE to proceed. This prevents reentering calls with only stipend gas from modifying state. The boundary condition (> not >=) must be exact.

Full block validation required: difficulty must match expected calculation (with bomb delay offset), PoW must verify against difficulty target, block rewards must match 2 ETH base (post-Constantinople). Invalid blocks must be rejected.
All incoming byte data must pass length validation before being cast to typed values. Exactly 20 bytes for Address, 32 bytes for Root, 256 bytes for Bloom. Rejection on mismatch.

Message origin must be validated. Response must have exactly one of result or error. Provider info (name, icon) must be sanitized before rendering to prevent XSS. Multiple wallet responses must be handled safely.
DApps should not blindly trust the injected provider. The provider could emit false connect/disconnect events or return incorrect chainId. DApps must validate critical data independently.
Wallet must not leak sensitive data to arbitrary DApp listeners. Listener callback exceptions must not crash the provider. Event data must not include private keys or signing material.
Connect/disconnect events are derived from network state which can be manipulated. DApps must handle rapid state transitions gracefully and not assume persistent connectivity.

Full block validation required: ancestry verification, temporal validity (slot <= current slot), finalization constraints, state transition execution. Block must not be accepted into fork choice store without passing all checks.
CL must handle EL responses defensively. A false is_inclusion_list_satisfied response could allow censoring proposers to bypass inclusion list enforcement. EL payload validity must be cross-checked.

EL must validate RANDAO value range (>2^64 confirms PoS context), withdrawal sequence constraints (max 16, ordered by index), and payload structural integrity. JWT authentication required but content validation essential.
Must validate: committee membership, BLS signature, timing (before VIEW_FREEZE_CUTOFF at 75% of slot), transaction content validity. Late inclusion lists must be rejected.

Full parameter validation: mutual exclusion of transaction/hash parameters, standard transaction validation if tx provided, resource limits on subscription count/duration. Privacy consideration: node operators can observe monitoring patterns.
Address range resolution must correctly distinguish EIP vs RIP precompile spaces. No address collision between ranges. On L1, calls to RIP range addresses should behave as calls to empty accounts.

Proposer can bias RANDAO by 1 bit through selective withholding (forfeiting rewards). System accepts this as known limitation. Applications using PREVRANDAO must implement commit-reveal with multi-epoch delays. RANDAO value is propagated to EL via mixHash.

Signature must be verified against fixed Capella fork domain (CAPELLA_FORK_VERSION). Cross-fork replay is acceptable by design. Exits only initiate exit process, no fund transfer. Post-EIP-7044, exits signed with non-Capella domains must be rejected.

Endpoint should be network-restricted to authorized monitoring systems only. Exposed metrics (sync status, peer count, block height) provide operational intelligence that could aid attack timing. No authentication mechanism defined in EIP-2159.
All blocks and transactions from P2P must be fully validated. Eclipse attack mitigations required. Invalid data must be rejected without corrupting local state.
All proposals and attestations must be validated against consensus rules. Conflicting attestations trigger slashing. Censorship attempts mitigated by inclusion list enforcement (EIP-7805).

Relay-provided blocks must be fully validated. Relay data is untrusted. Particularly relevant with Gloas builder registry: builders onboarded via deposits must be verified through withdrawal credential classification and prior-signature checks to prevent unauthorized builder registration.

All light client headers must pass: (1) blob gas field validation for pre-Deneb epochs (must be zero), (2) execution payload emptiness check for pre-Capella epochs, (3) Merkle branch verification of execution root against beacon body root. Headers from any source are fully untrusted.

Block header excess_blob_gas must exactly match calc_excess_blob_gas computation with timestamp-based fork boundary reset. Mismatch must result in block rejection. Special attention needed at fork boundary where excess_blob_gas resets to 0.

Input must be exactly 213 bytes. Final flag byte must be exactly 0 or 1. Gas cost = rounds * 1 must be available. High rounds values (up to 2^32-1) are valid but gas-metered. All input fields (h, m, t, f) are attacker-controlled and must produce deterministic RFC 7693 output.

The block_access_list_root provided by EL must be validated by CL. At fork transition it is initialized to Root() (zero). Post-fork, CL must verify EL-provided values are consistent with execution payload content.

JWT authentication required. ForkchoiceState must be validated: headBlockHash must reference a known valid payload, safeBlockHash must be ancestor of head, finalizedBlockHash must be consistent. Payload attributes must have valid timestamp. Message ordering must be enforced sequentially.

All requests must present a valid JWT bearer token signed with the shared secret. Invalid or missing JWT must result in immediate rejection. The shared secret must be securely generated and stored. Communication should occur over localhost or trusted network.

DApp-provided ABIs are untrusted. Wallets must: (1) validate interface spec version, (2) perform case-sensitive address matching, (3) optionally verify against trusted ABI database, (4) clearly indicate to users when ABI source is unverified. Decoded calldata display must not be presented as authoritative.

Wallets must assume all DApp-provided ABIs could be misleading. Users must be warned that decoded transaction details are only as trustworthy as the providing DApp. Wallets should indicate verified vs. unverified ABI sources visually.

User approval drives transaction signing. Wallet must present accurate information about trust level of decoded data. Users may be misled by malicious ABIs; wallet UI must distinguish verified from unverified decoded calldata.

Database responses are delivered over HTTPS. Database may not have entries for all contracts. Absence of verification does not imply malicious intent. Wallet must handle missing entries gracefully and indicate unverified status to user.

Full validation pipeline required: (1) correct subnet routing (column_index % SUBNET_COUNT == subnet_id), (2) temporal bounds (not future, within finalized range), (3) proposer signature verification, (4) KZG commitments inclusion Merkle proof, (5) batch KZG proof verification, (6) proposer index matches expected shuffling. REJECT for cryptographic failures, IGNORE for timing issues.

Request parameters must be validated: start_slot and count within data_column_serve_range, request size within MAX_REQUEST_BLOCKS_DENEB limits, block_root since minimum_request_epoch. Oversized requests must be rejected. Resource unavailability (code 3) returned for data outside serve range.

Input must contain only valid hex characters (0-9, a-f, A-F) after optional 0x prefix. Fixed-size outputs enforce exact byte lengths via padding. Type wrappers (U8, U64, U256) must enforce bounds checking. Invalid input must raise handled exceptions, not crash the node.

EL must fully validate execution payload content including block_access_list size, RLP encoding, and all header fields. JWT authentication ensures channel integrity but does not guarantee payload correctness.
EL must validate all withdrawal fields (U64 index, U64 validator_index, Address, U256 amount). Must not credit arbitrary amounts. JWT-authenticated channel but content validation required.
Must validate fork digest before SSZ deserialization. Must cryptographically verify sync committee signatures. Must reject malformed messages and apply peer scoring penalties.
Must validate fork version, SSZ deserialization, and cryptographic proofs on all responses. At least one honest peer must be available for security guarantees.
Deposit contract validates on-chain. CL must validate deposit data from Merkle tree including pubkey, withdrawal credentials, amount, and BLS signature before processing.
Must recalculate deposit root from finalized hashes and compare to transmitted deposit_root. Must verify against weak subjectivity checkpoint. Invalid snapshots must be rejected.

Full block header validation required: parent_hash, ommers_hash (empty), state_root, transactions_root, receipt_root, withdrawals_root, blob_gas_used, excess_blob_gas, parent_beacon_block_root. Invalid headers must be rejected.
Testnet reset period must be shorter than validator takeover timeline. For 10k genesis validators, reset period must be < 5.7 days. EIP-6916 reset mechanism provides the defense.

Must validate box structure (value, primaryType, types properties present). Must validate inner type definitions follow EIP-712 rules. Must enforce type isolation (inner types cannot reference outer types). Must render box contents to user for informed consent.
Full transaction validation required: signature verification, nonce check, gas limit validation, value bounds, calldata parsing. No authentication required for public RPC endpoints.
All blocks and transactions received from peers must be fully validated. Eclipse attack mitigation required (diverse peer connections). Invalid data must result in peer scoring penalties.

All validator messages must be cryptographically verified (BLS signatures). Conflicting attestations must trigger slashing conditions. Censorship resistance depends on sufficient honest validator participation.

Checkpoint data must be verified against known weak subjectivity checkpoint. In EIP-6916, genesis_0 parameters must be hardcoded and correct. Compromised endpoints could provide fraudulent genesis state.

Full validation of request schema, version, chainId format, call array structure, bundle size limits, capability support, atomicity requirements, and duplicate ID detection. Application identity must be verified to prevent cross-app status leakage.
Authorization check (error 4100 if unauthorized). Capability filtering for untrusted callers to prevent wallet fingerprinting. Address must match enabled account.
Sensitive capabilities must be filtered for untrusted callers. Response must not uniquely identify wallet type or configuration.

Speed-up invariants must be validated: same nonce, recipient, value, data with minimum 10% gas increase. Cancel must construct valid self-send. User approval UI must accurately represent transaction details.

Events must be scoped per-application to prevent cross-app information leakage. Event data (oldTx, newTx, nonce, from) must be accurate. Replacement type classification (speedup vs cancel vs generic) must be correct.

All three length fields must be validated <= 1024 bytes per EIP-7823. Gas cost must accurately reflect computation complexity. Zero modulus, zero exponent, zero base edge cases must be handled. Short input must be zero-padded. Output must be exactly modulus_length bytes.

Inputs with any length field > 1024 bytes must be immediately rejected. All gas allocated to the call must be consumed on violation. Error status must be returned. Length check must occur before complex gas pricing calculation.

Stack depth must be validated (depth <= 1024). Contract creation must check address collision, validate no 0xEF prefix, enforce MAX_CODE_SIZE (24576 bytes), charge code deposit gas. ExceptionalHalt must consume all gas. Revert must preserve gas but rollback state. EIP-7702 authorizations must be properly validated.

Block must be validated against correct fork rules determined by block number (pre-merge) or timestamp (post-merge). Fork criteria ordering must be deterministic. Constantinople activation at correct network-specific block heights. Invalid blocks must be rejected.

Block at or above fork threshold must activate all constituent EIPs atomically. Timestamp-based activation (post-merge) must account for potential timestamp manipulation. All 5 Constantinople EIPs must activate simultaneously at fork block.

Full envelope structure validation: [Expiry(4), TTL(4), Topic(4), Data(var), Nonce(8)]. PoW must meet minimum requirement and not be NaN/INF/negative. Topic must match bloom filter. Protocol violations must trigger peer disconnection. Unknown packet codes must be silently ignored.
Message encryption (ECIES or AES-GCM) and ECDSA signing must be applied correctly. 256-byte padding must be applied to prevent size-based metadata leakage.

Blob KZG commitment count must not exceed get_blob_parameters(epoch).max_blobs_per_block. The BLOB_SCHEDULE lookup must correctly find the largest scheduled epoch <= current epoch. All nodes must agree on BLOB_SCHEDULE configuration to prevent network partitioning.

Builder BLS signature must be verified. Bid value must be validated against builder's beacon balance. Blockhash commitment must be well-formed. Builder equivocation (multiple headers for same slot) must be tolerated without consensus failure.

Full multi-stage validation required: BLS signature, blockhash match against committed header, execution state transition validity, withdrawals root match, beacon state root match. Any failure must reject the envelope.

PTC member must be in the assigned PTC for the slot. Attestation signature must be verified. Individual attestations do not determine payload status - only aggregate threshold (>=256/512) is authoritative.
Fork choice must resist reorg attempts by proposers with >20% stake controlling consecutive slots. Unconditional proposer payment (deducted at commitment time) is the primary safety property.

Full collision detection required before init code execution: target address nonce must be 0 AND code length must be 0. Collision triggers invalid opcode exception consuming all gas and reverting state.

EL trusts CL-provided beacon root without independent verification. Root is stored via system call to beacon roots contract. Content validation relies entirely on CL consensus integrity. Ring buffer index (timestamp % 8191) must prevent stale data access via timestamp matching.

Beacon roots contract: input must be exactly 32 bytes, non-zero, and timestamp must match stored timestamp at computed index. Ecrecover: v must be 27 or 28, r and s must be in range (0, SECP256K1N). Invalid inputs return empty output (no revert). Callers must handle empty return correctly.

Read-only informational endpoint with no consensus implications. Response format validation only (valid JSON-RPC string). No content verification possible - wallets should cross-reference with chain ID.

Node operator controls response content. Symbol cannot be verified against any authoritative source. Wallets must treat as informational only and not rely on it for security-critical network identification.

Permission request must display full scope to user (chain ID, contract, functions, duration). Permission secret must be cryptographically random (>=128 bits entropy). Every silent transaction must verify: (1) secret matches, (2) permission not expired, (3) transaction within permitted contract/function scope. Secret leakage enables unauthorized transactions until expiry.

Deposit amount must be exactly 32 ETH. Validator pubkey and withdrawal credentials must be valid. Activation rate bounded by MAX_PER_EPOCH_ACTIVATION_CHURN_LIMIT (8) to prevent exponential validator set growth. Queue ordering is FIFO.

Block RLP-encoded size must be validated against MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE (8,388,608 bytes) before expensive processing. Handshake must validate networkId, genesis hash, and forkId. Data availability bitmask claims must not be trusted without verification.

Transaction gasLimit must be validated against cap of 16,777,216 (2^24) at both mempool acceptance and block validation. Contract creation transactions must pass EIP-684 + EIP-7610 collision/storage checks.

Hash functions accept arbitrary byte inputs. Security relies on Keccak collision resistance and preimage resistance. Hash output is trusted as deterministic identifier of input. All client implementations must produce identical results.

Block environmental data (timestamp, coinbase, PREVRANDAO) is set by block proposer within protocol constraints. PREVRANDAO should not be treated as secure randomness. Timestamp manipulation within ~15 second bounds is possible. For historical PoW: Ethash verification required (hash <= target difficulty).

Three-way validation required: (1) target nonce == 0, (2) target code length == 0, (3) target storage is empty (EIP-7610 addition). Failure triggers revert as invalid opcode. This prevents code overwriting and residual storage exploitation for all 28 known mainnet addresses with pre-EIP-161 residual storage.

Size check must occur early in validation pipeline before expensive operations (signature verification, state transition). MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE (8 MiB) provides 2 MiB safety margin below CL's ~10 MiB limit. Transaction gas cap independently prevents single-transaction resource exhaustion.

Full transaction validation required: signature recovery, nonce check, EIP-3607 sender code hash check (CodeHash == EMPTYCODEHASH), gas limit validation with EIP-1884 repriced opcodes, balance sufficiency check.
Trace requests must be rate-limited. eth_call/eth_estimateGas bypass EIP-3607 checks for simulation purposes. Resource consumption must be bounded to prevent DoS.

All transactions in received blocks must pass EIP-3607 sender validation. Block difficulty must be recomputed using EIP-100 formula. Timestamp bounds must be enforced. Blocks with invalid transactions must be rejected entirely.

Messages must pass: (1) REJECT checks: tx size <= MAX_BYTES_PER_INCLUSION_LIST, valid slot, committee membership, BLS signature verification. (2) IGNORE checks: timing constraints, committee root match, per-validator submission limit (max 2 per slot). REJECT failures penalize peer score.
Request parameters (slot, committee_indices bitvector) must be validated. Response size bounded to MAX_REQUEST_INCLUSION_LIST (16). Must not serve stale or unvalidated inclusion lists.

All JSON messages must be validated for format, type, and hex encoding. Worker credentials must be verified. Session IDs must be unpredictable. Error counts must be tracked with maxerrors disconnect threshold. Idle timeout must be enforced.
Solution submissions must validate: worker token authorization, job ID matches active job, nonce validity, and hash meets target difficulty. Stale/invalid submissions increment error counter.
Mining clients should validate epoch parameters, target difficulty values, extranonce bounds (max 6 bytes), and header hash format. Stale job indicators must be honored.

All messages must pass: JSON format validation (LF terminated), message type classification (request/response/notification), hex format validation (lowercase, no 0x prefix, minimal digits). Invalid messages return error codes: 2xx conditional, 3xx auth, 4xx syntax, 5xx server.

Block timestamp must be within acceptable bounds relative to parent (used in EIP-100 difficulty calculation). Uncle references must be cryptographically verifiable via unclesHash. PREVRANDAO source must be the parent beacon block randao_mix. Difficulty must match EIP-100 formula: max((uncle_factor) - ((timestamp - parent.timestamp) // 9), -99).

After nonce verification, sender's CodeHash must be checked against EMPTYCODEHASH (0xc5d2460186f7233c927e7db2dcc703c0e500b653ca82273b7bfad8045d85a470). Any transaction from an address with deployed code must be rejected. This check must be applied consistently across all clients to prevent consensus failures.

Wallet must faithfully display typed data to user. Domain separator must include chainId and verifyingContract. User must approve signing. Application-level replay protection (nonces) is NOT provided by EIP-712 and must be implemented separately.

ForkID must be validated per EIP-2124: compute local forkHash from genesis + fork blocks, compare with remote. Incompatible peers must be disconnected immediately. Peers may lie about forkid to waste connection slots.
Blocks must be validated against the correct fork rules based on block height. Fork-specific validation (Frontier vs Homestead vs later) must be applied correctly. Invalid blocks must be rejected.

ENR validation: size <= 300 bytes, valid RLP, sorted unique keys, valid secp256k1 signature over keccak256 of content. Sequence number must be checked for freshness. Unknown identity schemes must be rejected.

ENR records from DNS must pass full cryptographic validation. DNS responses themselves are untrusted (potential spoofing). DNSSEC provides additional protection but is not required. Impact of DNS spoofing limited to DoS due to ENR signature verification.

ENR records from ENS must pass full cryptographic validation. On-chain data integrity depends on Ethereum consensus. Resolver contracts could be compromised. ENR signature verification provides final trust anchor.

Domain separator prevents cross-contract and cross-chain replay. Same-domain replay prevention requires application-level nonce tracking. Verifying contracts must correctly implement EIP-712 encoding and check domain separator fields.

JWT-authenticated channel. EL must produce execution payloads that include exactly the specified withdrawals. Content validation: withdrawal amounts, validator indices, and execution addresses must match CL state. A malicious CL could specify incorrect withdrawals.

Pre-fork (Deneb) format data must be locally upgraded to Electra format using upgrade functions. Merkle branches must be normalized using Electra generalized indices. All cryptographic verification (sync committee signatures) must pass after format conversion.
Version negotiation must complete before compressed messages are processed. Peer hello messages must be validated for protocol version compatibility.
Decompressed message size must be validated against 16MB limit before allocation. Snappy varint must be checked for overflow. Decompression failures must result in message rejection.
Block difficulty must be recomputed and compared against claimed value. Fork activation rules (Arrow Glacier block number) must be correctly applied. Invalid blocks must be rejected.

Full transaction validation required: type byte, RLP decoding, field count, chain ID, signature verification, access list structure (20-byte addresses, 32-byte keys), and gas calculation (including access list costs). Malformed transactions must be rejected.
Response must correctly include or exclude baseFee field based on EIP-1559 fork activation status of the queried block. Invalid block hashes must return null.
KZG commitment count must not exceed MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK_ELECTRA. Block must pass all fork choice assertions (parent exists, timing valid, finalization lineage, data availability).
SingleAttestation data.index must equal 0. Attester must be verified as a member of the committee for the given slot. Duplicate attestations must be rejected.
Blob index and KZG commitments must be validated against MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK_ELECTRA. KZG proofs must be batch-verified. Request sizes must not exceed MAX_REQUEST_BLOB_SIDECARS_ELECTRA.

Authenticated via JWT but content must be validated. Inclusion list transactions from the execution engine must be structurally valid. A compromised EL could return empty or manipulated lists, undermining censorship resistance.
PayloadAttributes including parent_beacon_block_root (EIP-4788) must be validated. The execution engine must faithfully construct payloads per the provided attributes.

Valid jump destinations must be pre-computed by scanning bytecode and correctly skipping PUSH data bytes. JUMP/JUMPI must validate destinations against this whitelist. Invalid jumps must halt execution and consume all gas.

Varint size must be checked against 2^32-1 limit. Decompressed size must be validated against 16MB limit BEFORE decompression to prevent memory exhaustion. Connection must be terminated on overflow detection.

Announced metadata (hash, type, size, address, nonce) is UNVERIFIED and must only be used as optimization hints, never for security decisions. Full transaction must be retrieved and independently validated. Protocol violations (metadata mismatch) must result in peer penalization.

Blocks received from peers must be fully validated (header, PoW/PoS, state transitions, gas limits). Block size may be larger due to cheaper calldata (EIP-2028); propagation delays must not exceed security bounds.

Full transaction validation required: intrinsic gas check (EIP-2028 calldata pricing), blob count limits (max 6 per EIP-7594), cell proof verification (KZG batch verify), versioned hash matching. Reject transactions failing any check.

All received column samples must have KZG proofs batch-verified against known commitments. Insufficient valid samples indicate data withholding. Node ID manipulation for custody concentration must be mitigated. Reconstruction requires >=50% of columns.

Sync committee messages must be signature-verified. Aggregators must verify beacon_block_root consistency. Best contribution selection must use highest signature count. Clock synchronization assumed for 1/3 and 2/3 slot timing deadlines.

Blocks must be validated against the correct consensus ruleset based on block number (e.g., EIP-1588 fork boundary at 7280000). PoW verification must use the appropriate algorithm. Blocks with excessive calldata must not degrade network propagation below security bounds.

EOF containers must pass full structural validation (magic bytes, header, sections), code validation (valid opcodes, EIP-3670), static stack analysis (no underflow/overflow, EIP-5450), and function call validation (CALLF/RETF/JUMPF, EIP-4750/6206). Both initcode and deployed code must be validated. Invalid containers must be rejected at deploy time.

JWT authentication verifies channel identity. Execution payloads received via newPayload must be independently validated by the EL (state transition, gas limits, transaction validity). Fork choice updates must be validated against EL's view of the chain. SYNCING status must be handled gracefully.

JWT authentication verifies channel identity. Execution payloads returned by the EL must be structurally valid. The CL validator must verify payload fits within beacon block constraints. If execution engine returns SYNCING or error, the validator should skip block proposal for safety.

All received beacon blocks must pass beacon state transition validation AND execution payload validation (via Engine API). Attestations must be signature-verified. Invalid blocks/attestations must be rejected. Peers sending invalid data should be penalized.

Full transaction validation required: type detection (legacy/0x01/0x02), RLP decode, signature verification, nonce check, gas limit check, max_fee_per_gas >= base_fee_per_gas (EIP-1559), access list format validation, intrinsic gas calculation including access list costs.

Input validation for block hash format and uncle index. Response must correctly include or omit baseFee field based on EIP-1559 fork activation status. Malformed inputs must not cause crashes or information leakage.

Chain switch requests must be validated: chainId format (0x-prefixed EIP-155), RPC URL sanitization (block private IPs, require HTTPS), cross-check against known chain database for phishing detection. User confirmation required before any chain switch. Error 4001 on rejection.

SSRF prevention: block localhost, private IP ranges (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x), link-local addresses. Validate URL format. Verify net_version and eth_chainId responses match the claimed chain. Timeout enforcement to prevent resource exhaustion.

Builder bid validation required: cryptographic signature verification, builder balance coverage check (sufficient funds to cover bid amount), parent block hash consistency with current chain head, bid validity period. Proposer must fall back to local block construction if no valid bids received.

All received DataColumnSidecars must be verified against KZG commitments and proofs before acceptance into the local data store. Invalid sidecars must be rejected. Column indices must match the subscribed subnet.

Fallback column retrieval from peers requires same KZG proof verification as gossip-received data. Peers may be unresponsive (timeout handling needed) or serve invalid data. Recovery threshold of >=50% columns must be met before attempting Reed-Solomon reconstruction.

Full node must correctly construct LightClientHeaders with accurate execution payload headers and valid Merkle branch proofs. Light clients must verify execution branch proofs against trusted beacon block body roots. Fork-dependent header format (Capella vs pre-Capella) must be correctly applied.

All byte inputs must be validated before cryptographic operations: 48-byte inputs must be valid BLS12-381 G1 points (check point at infinity special case, then full BLS validation), 32-byte inputs must be less than BLS modulus, input lengths must be exactly 48 or 32 bytes as expected. Trusted setup parameter KZG_SETUP_G2_MONOMIAL_1 must not be compromised.

All blocks and transactions received from peers must undergo full validation: block header validation, transaction signature verification, state transition execution, gas accounting (including EIP-1559 effective gas price calculation, 20% refund cap). Eclipse attack mitigation through peer diversity.

Attestations must be validated for correct signature, slot, committee assignment, and beacon block root. Payload timeliness attestations (Gloas) must be from valid PTC members. data.index field (repurposed for payload status signaling: 0=absent, 1=present) must be validated. Conflicting attestations trigger slashing conditions.
Full transaction validation required including access list structure, gas pricing for warm/cold slots, and intrinsic gas calculation. Malformed access lists must be rejected.
Identity precompile performs no input validation by design—gas cost must scale with input size to prevent resource amplification. Output is untrusted pass-through data.

Input signature parameters (v, r, s) must be validated: v must be 27 or 28, r and s must be in range (0, SECP256K1N). Invalid inputs must return empty output without reverting. Cryptographic library must be correctly implemented.

Gas cost must be calculated before execution using EIP-2565 formula: max(200, floor(complexity * iteration_count / 3)). Input lengths parsed from calldata must be validated. Minimum gas floor of 200 prevents spam.
Minimum gas floor of 200 must be enforced. Gas formula must accurately reflect actual computation cost across all client implementations to prevent underpricing attacks.

Full block structure validation required: header conformance to fork rules, state trie updates, bloom filter computation, and transaction execution. Invalid blocks must be rejected without state corruption.

Checkpoint format must be parsed and validated: block root must match canonical chain at specified epoch. If checkpoint epoch > finalized epoch, block must exist in canonical chain. If checkpoint epoch <= finalized epoch, root must match. Invalid checkpoints must cause client termination with descriptive error.

Conflicting finalized checkpoints require at least 1/3 of total stake to be slashable. WS checkpoint must reject attacker forks. Safety margin of at least 1/3 - SAFETY_DECAY/100 (~23.3%) must be maintained within the WS period.

Each data column sidecar must pass: (1) batched KZG commitment verification, (2) inclusion proof verification. Invalid columns must be rejected and validation failures tracked via metrics. Reconstruction of missing columns must only use verified data.
Full block validation required: header fields, gas limit bounds, PoW/PoS validity, transaction execution correctness, state root verification. All data from peers is potentially malicious.

Peers may lie about transaction types and sizes. Node must validate array length consistency (types, sizes, hashes same length), apply throttling policies based on announced sizes, and verify actual transaction data after fetch.

Full transaction validation required. Timeout parameter must be bounded by node-configured maximum to prevent resource exhaustion. Node must handle concurrent synchronous connections without blocking consensus operations.
All transaction fields must be validated: sufficient gas available in block, exact nonce match, sender balance covers gas*price + value, sender is EOA. Invalid transactions must be rejected.

Contract validates deposit_data_root integrity, minimum deposit amount, and parameter lengths (pubkey=48, withdrawal_credentials=32, signature=96 bytes). BLS signature verification is NOT performed at this boundary - it is deferred to CL. Invalid BLS signatures result in burned ETH.

CL must perform full BLS12-381 signature verification on all deposits read from the deposit contract. Invalid signatures must be silently ignored without affecting chain state. The progressive Merkle tree root must be verified.

All RPC responses must include cryptographic proofs (Merkle proofs against known state roots). Proofs must be verified for both correctness and completeness. Providers with invalid proofs must be flagged as malicious.
Query results must include completeness proofs. The 2D log index must provide bounded false-positive guarantees. System must handle potentially expensive queries without DoS.

Wallet must display validator address and data to user for approval before signing. Message must be prefixed with 0x19 || 0x00 || validatorAddress to ensure domain separation. Signature cannot be replayed across different validators or as a transaction.

Validator must reconstruct message using its own address (not a supplied address), compute keccak256 hash, and use ecrecover to verify the signer. Must not accept signatures intended for other validators.

Input must be exactly 213 bytes. Final flag must be 0 or 1. Gas cost is rounds * GAS_BLAKE2_PER_ROUND, preventing resource exhaustion for high round counts. Invalid inputs must raise InvalidParameter exception.

Full header validation: parent hash, gas limit within parent +/- 1/1024 and >= 5000, timestamp, difficulty per formula with bomb. PoW: hashimoto_light verification, mix_digest match, result <= MAX_VALUE/difficulty. Max 2 ommers, age 1-6 blocks.

Full transaction validation required: decode transaction type, verify signature bounds (r, s within SECP256K1 curve order), recover sender, validate gas sufficiency, check nonce overflow (< 2^64-1), enforce init code size limit (MAX_INIT_CODE_SIZE), and compute intrinsic gas costs.
Block number parameter must be validated. baseFee field inclusion must be conditional on fork status. Response must not leak internal state beyond what is publicly available.

Flow control parameters must be validated: schema validation, capability scope checks, rollback-none atomicity conflict detection. Wallet must correctly implement requested atomicity and failure handling semantics.

Full block validation required: header validation (number, timestamp, gas, difficulty, parent hash), fork-specific checks (DAO extra data marker in 10-block window), gas cost enforcement per fork rules (Istanbul, Tangerine Whistle repricing), 63/64 call gas allocation.

Messages must be checked against broadcast file if loaded. Conflicting messages (different signature for same validator) must be rejected. Messages for unknown validators must be accepted normally. BLS signature verification required.

Blob KZG commitment count must be <= MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK (6). Versioned hashes must be validated against execution payload blob transactions via is_valid_versioned_hashes. Execution payload must be forwarded to EL via Engine API for validation.

JWT authentication must be verified. Execution payload content must be fully validated: versioned hash consistency with blob commitments, parent beacon block root correctness, blob gas metrics accuracy. The EL must not blindly trust CL-provided payload data.

JWT authentication must be verified. CL must handle both VALID and INVALID responses correctly. blob_gas_used and excess_blob_gas values cached in beacon state header must be validated for consistency.

BLS signatures must be cryptographically verified. Voluntary exits must use fixed CAPELLA_FORK_VERSION domain for signature validation (EIP-7044). Validator index must be active. Only one BLSToExecutionChange per validator. Attestation inclusion window must respect MIN_ATTESTATION_INCLUSION_DELAY and extended epoch rules (EIP-7045).

Input validation required: input length check, Fp/Fp2 field element encoding (top 16 bytes zero, value < modulus), point-on-curve verification, subgroup membership for MSM/pairing. Gas must be correctly computed (fixed for ADD/MAP, variable with discount for MSM, linear for pairing). All validation failures must consume all provided gas.

ENRRequest must be rejected if no prior ping exchange exists (amplification attack prevention). Request expiration timestamp must be in the future. ENRResponse signature must be verified via secp256k1. Request hash must match pending request. ENR sequence numbers in ping/pong must be correctly compared.

Broadcast file content must be validated: BLS signatures must be verified for each entry, validator indices must correspond to active validators. File integrity should be verified before loading. Conflicting entries in the file should be detected.
Input data is arbitrary bytes. Gas metering (GAS_RIPEMD160 + GAS_RIPEMD160_WORD * words) must accurately reflect computation cost to prevent DoS. Output is deterministic 32-byte padded hash.
All precompile inputs are untrusted. Each precompile must independently validate input format and charge appropriate gas before performing computation.
Proof must be verified against a trusted root. Proof length must match generalized index depth. Reconstructed root must exactly equal expected root. SHA-256 collision resistance is assumed.
Helper indices must be computed independently from provided data. Proof length must equal helper_indices length. All leaf positions must be valid for the SSZ type schema.
Full transaction validation required. Transaction type byte must be checked against RIP range (0x40-0x7f) to prevent misrouting. EIP-2718 envelope format must be validated.
L1 nodes must reject or ignore RIP transaction types. Namespace boundary (0x40-0x7f inclusive) must be strictly enforced to prevent type collision between EIP and RIP definitions.
Attestation slot must be verified against extended window (up to last slot of epoch N+1). Target epoch must be current or previous. Signature must be valid. Duplicate attestations must be rejected.
Attestation must pass extended gossip window check before propagation. Stale attestations (beyond epoch N+1) must be dropped. Rate limiting may be needed to prevent gossip flooding.
Block validator must verify all included attestations are within the extended inclusion window. TIMELY_TARGET_FLAG is set without inclusion_delay constraint for valid attestations.

JWT authentication validates channel integrity but not payload correctness. CL must handle all three responses (VALID, NOT_VALIDATED, INVALIDATED) correctly. latestValidHash must be used to scope invalidation. SAFE_SLOTS_TO_IMPORT_OPTIMISTICALLY (128) provides merge block protection.

Blocks imported optimistically are added to optimistic_roots set. Validator duties MUST be restricted while head is optimistic (no DOMAIN_BEACON_PROPOSER, DOMAIN_BEACON_ATTESTER, DOMAIN_SYNC_COMMITTEE signing).

SAFE_SLOTS_TO_IMPORT_OPTIMISTICALLY provides 128-slot window for honest chain to justify. Honest chain with higher justified checkpoint must override poisoned store. CLI override available as last resort.

File content must be parsed and validated: hex values checked for format, addresses validated as 20-byte B_20, balances validated as U256. Chain_id must match expected network. Corrupted or tampered genesis files must cause initialization failure.

Request must be authenticated. BLS domain must be validated (beacon_proposer, beacon_attester, randao only). Key identifier must exist. JSON body must contain all required fields. Slashing protection must be enforced externally. Rate limiting required for DoS protection.
HSM must be properly configured with access controls. Keys must be zeroized from memory after signing. Physical access to signer node must be restricted.
TLS/HTTPS must be used to prevent eavesdropping on signatures and signing requests. Without encryption, signatures could be intercepted enabling replay or analysis attacks.
Block number must be checked against fork activation threshold. Correct rule set (pre-Berlin vs post-Berlin) must be applied. Applying wrong rules could accept invalid blocks or reject valid ones.

Full request validation required: rate limiting for eth_config (recommended 1s interval), transaction format validation, authorization tuple validation for type-4 transactions. Access should be restricted to trusted interfaces where possible.
Rate limiting must be enforced to prevent DDoS. Endpoint access should be restricted to trusted interfaces only. Configuration data exposure is an information leak risk.

Full cryptographic validation required: blob index < MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK, correct subnet mapping, valid proposer signature, valid Merkle inclusion proof, valid KZG proof, blob_kzg_commitments count <= MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK.
Enforce MAX_REQUEST_BLOB_SIDECARS (768) limit. Verify requested slots are within MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS retention window. Return ResourceUnavailable error for out-of-window requests.

Bootstrap must be verified against trusted block root (out-of-band). Updates require valid sync committee aggregate signatures (>= 2/3 threshold). Finality updates must contain valid finality proof. Light client must verify all data cryptographically before accepting.
Configuration data from any single node must be cross-checked against multiple sources and the official specification. Never trust a single node's configuration response for fork readiness decisions.

STATICCALL (EIP-214) enforces read-only execution: CREATE, LOG, SSTORE, SELFDESTRUCT, CALL-with-value are prohibited. STATIC flag must propagate correctly through nested calls. For EIP-7702 delegated EOAs, delegation resolves only one level. Precompile inputs (EIP-1108) must be validated: point-on-curve check, input length validation.

Type-4 transaction validation: non-empty authorization list, non-null destination, sender must be EOA or delegated. Each authorization: chain_id must be 0 or current, nonce < 2^64-1, valid ecrecover with MAGIC prefix, s <= secp256k1n/2, authority code empty or existing delegation, authority nonce matches.

Nonce-based replay protection: authority nonce is incremented after each successful authorization, so replayed tuples will fail nonce match. Cross-chain replay is possible if chain_id=0 was used in the original authorization.

All externally sourced historical data must be validated against known canonical block hashes, transaction roots, and receipt roots. Data integrity verification is mandatory before serving to RPC clients.

All received transactions must be fully validated (signature, nonce, gas, initcode size per EIP-3860). Blob transactions received without sidecars must not be forwarded until all blobs are fetched and validated (EIP-8094).

Blob data received via PooledBlobs must have hash correspondence validated against requested vhashes. Missing or mismatched blobs must be handled gracefully. Nodes MUST NOT forward transactions with unvalidated blobs.

All P2P messages must use correct fork version encoding (EIP-7928). Messages with incorrect fork versions must be rejected. Fork version is determined by epoch threshold checks in strict descending order.

Full transaction validation required: signature verification, chain ID check (EIP-155 replay protection), initcode size <= 49152 bytes for creation transactions (EIP-3860), gas limit >= intrinsic gas including initcode cost, contract code size <= 24KB (EIP-170).

CL relies on EL to correctly execute and validate payloads. The Engine API channel is JWT-authenticated. CL still validates parent_hash consistency, RANDAO, timestamp, and no-empty-transactions constraint independently before delegating full execution validation to EL (Bellatrix).

EL must validate execution payload content (transaction validity, state transitions, gas accounting) regardless of CL authentication. JWT authentication ensures channel integrity but not content correctness.
Proposed blocks must pass full validation: execution payload checks (parent hash, RANDAO, timestamp), signature verification, slot/epoch consistency. Equivocating proposers must be slashed.

Relay is expected to return valid, highest-value bids and reveal full payloads after proposer commitment. Proposer should implement fallback to local block building if relay is unresponsive. Relay failure after signing results in missed slot (liveness risk).
Builder payloads must be validated by the relay before being presented to proposers. Invalid payloads, censored blocks, or undervalued bids should be filtered by relay validation.
Searcher bundles are untrusted transaction orderings. Standard transaction validation applies to all individual transactions within bundles.

Slashing evidence must be cryptographically verified (conflicting signatures from same validator). Reporter identity is irrelevant — evidence validity is independently verifiable. Bellatrix parameters: MIN_SLASHING_PENALTY_QUOTIENT=32, PROPORTIONAL_SLASHING_MULTIPLIER=3.

Input must be exactly 160 bytes. Signature bounds (0 < r,s < n), public key field bounds (0 <= qx,qy < p), curve equation membership, and non-identity point checks are all required. Gas (6900) is consumed regardless of validation outcome. Signatures are malleable (both (r,s) and (r,n-s) valid) per EIP-7951.

Blocks must be validated against fork-specific rules. At block 2,675,000 (Spurious Dragon), EIP-155 replay protection, EIP-160 EXP cost, EIP-161 state clearing, and EIP-170 code size limits activate. All blocks must meet applicable rule set.

Block must pass: correct slot > parent slot, correct parent root, correct proposer index, valid block signature, valid RANDAO reveal (BLS signature of epoch), valid ETH1 data vote, all operations validated (up to 16 proposer slashings, 2 attester slashings, 128 attestations, 16 deposits, 16 voluntary exits). State root must match after application.

Attestation target epoch must be current or previous epoch. Target root and beacon block root must be known in store. Target root must be consistent with checkpoint at target epoch. Equivocating validators (detected via on_attester_slashing) must be excluded from latest_messages updates.

Block must have known parent in store, slot not from future, must descend from finalized checkpoint. State transition must be applied and succeed. Timeliness recorded for proposer boost eligibility. Unrealized justified/finalized checkpoints updated.

Messages must be deserialized using correct fork-specific SSZ types. Nodes must reject messages from future forks they haven't activated. Light client finality and optimistic updates must be verified against sync committee signatures before acceptance.
Responses must use fork-appropriate SSZ types. Range requests must be chunked by fork boundary. Rate limiting should be applied to prevent resource exhaustion from excessive requests.

Merkle proof must be verified against eth1_data.deposit_root. BLS signature over DepositMessage must be verified. Invalid BLS signatures result in validator record creation with unusable keys. Deposit count must match expected sequential index.

Full block validation: sequential block numbers, timestamp ordering, gas limit within parent±1/1024 and ≥5000, base fee calculation per EIP-1559, blob gas pricing, PoS field validation. Body execution with Merkle root verification (transactions, receipts, withdrawals, state). Reject InvalidBlock on any failure.

Nonce match, sufficient balance, sender is EOA, EIP-1559 fee structure valid. For blob txs: versioned hash version 0x01, blob gas within limits. Gas refund capped at 20% of consumed. Priority fee paid to proposer. Empty accounts cleaned up.

Withdrawal data from CL is trusted (JWT-authenticated channel). EL must correctly convert amounts to Wei (multiply by 10^9), increase recipient balances, and update withdrawal trie. Withdrawal root must match header value.

Input must be exactly 192 bytes. Versioned hash must start with 0x01. Field elements z and y must be < BLS_MODULUS. Commitment and proof must be valid G1 curve points. KZG proof verification must use trusted library. Fixed gas cost 50000. Output is FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB and BLS_MODULUS on success.

Blob field elements must be < BLS_MODULUS. Evaluation challenge derived deterministically via Fiat-Shamir (FSBLOBVERIFY_V1_ domain). Polynomial evaluated at challenge using barycentric interpolation. KZG proof verified via pairing check. Batch verification uses separate domain (RCKZGBATCH___V1_).

Transaction gas limit must be >= max(standard_gas_cost, floor_gas_cost). Floor gas = 21000 + (10 × tokens_in_calldata). Tokens = zero_bytes + (nonzero_bytes × 4). Data-heavy transactions (floor > standard) pay 2.5x more per calldata byte. Gas estimation APIs must account for floor.

All 4096 field elements in the blob must be strictly < BLS_MODULUS. Field elements are parsed as 32-byte big-endian values. Commitment is computed as linear combination of trusted setup G1 points. Invalid field elements must cause rejection.

Commitment and proof must be valid G1 points (KeyValidate with identity permitted). Pairing check: e(P - y·G1, G2) == e(Q, X - z·G2). Batch verification uses Fiat-Shamir challenges with RCKZGBATCH___V1_ domain. All verification relies on trusted setup security and BLS12-381 hardness.

Evaluation challenge z derived deterministically from blob and commitment via Fiat-Shamir (FSBLOBVERIFY_V1_ domain). Polynomial evaluated at z using barycentric interpolation. Result verified against KZG proof via pairing check. Bit-reversal permutation applied to 4096-element domain.

Block parameter must be validated: detect format (hex string, tag, or object), validate mutual exclusivity of blockNumber/blockHash in object format, verify block existence (error -32001 if not found), check canonical status if requireCanonical=true (error -32000 if non-canonical). Historical state must be available for the requested block.

Object-format parameters must not contain both blockNumber and blockHash simultaneously. Parameter type detection must handle all three formats (hex, tag, object) without ambiguity. Invalid formats must return appropriate JSON-RPC errors.

Peer status must be validated: networkid, genesis hash, and forkid must match. Incompatible peers must be disconnected. The earliestBlock and latestBlock values are self-reported and cannot be trusted until verified by actual block requests.

Block range updates are rate-limited (max once per epoch/32 blocks). Range claims must be treated as unverified. Peers failing to serve blocks within claimed ranges should be penalized via peer scoring. No more than one update per epoch should be accepted.

Receipts in eth/69 format omit bloom filters. Receiving nodes must recompute bloom filters from logs if needed for local queries. Receipt data must be validated against expected block hashes. The compact format [tx-type, post-state-or-status, cumulative-gas, logs] must be correctly parsed.

Status message validation: networkid, genesis, forkid must match. blockRange is self-reported and unverified. Peer's claimed range must be stored but not trusted until validated by actual block requests.

Range responses may contain multiple [startBlock, endBlock] tuples representing non-contiguous ranges. Responses must be treated as unverified claims. Dishonest range claims detected via failed block requests should trigger peer scoring penalties. Sybil resistance depends on diverse peer selection.

Blocks must pass consensus-layer validation (slot, proposer, signature, parent) and execution payload timestamp check before propagation. Blocks with invalid execution payloads SHOULD NOT cause peer downscoring (prevents network segregation between optimistic and non-optimistic nodes). Message size up to 10 MiB due to ExecutionPayload.
Responses must use correct fork-version-appropriate SSZ schema (phase0, altair, or bellatrix) for each requested block. Response chunks limited to 10 MiB each. Fork version determined by block slot.

All column sidecars must be structurally verified via verify_data_column_sidecar and cryptographically verified via verify_data_column_sidecar_kzg_proofs. Retrieval failure triggers block queuing (not rejection). Data availability is guaranteed only within MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS window.

Blocks must pass sequential validation: parent exists in store, slot is valid, finality constraints met, data availability confirmed via DAS (is_data_available without blob_kzg_commitments). Only after all checks pass is state transition executed. Blocks failing DA check MAY be queued for later processing.
Full block validation required: header fields, transaction validity, state root verification, gas limit checks. All block data is untrusted.
Full transaction validation required: ECDSA signature recovery, nonce check, balance check, gas limit validation, RLP decoding. All transaction data is untrusted.
Full transaction validation plus 0xEF first-byte check on returned runtime bytecode. Init code execution must be gas-bounded. Exceptional abort on reserved 0xEF prefix.

Query parsing and schema validation required. Operation type must be checked (signing, compiling, mining operations denied). Input scalar types (Bytes32, Address, BigInt) must be format-validated. No built-in auth - external access control assumed.
RLP-encoded transaction must be decoded and fully validated before broadcast. Same validation as JSON-RPC transaction submission.

Root record signature must be verified against known secp256k1 public key. Sequence number must be >= cached value (anti-rollback). Branch content must match subdomain hash (keccak256). Multiple independent DNS sources should be used to mitigate eclipse attacks.

JWT authentication verifies channel identity. Execution payload content must be fully validated: deprecated PoW fields (difficulty=0, nonce=0, ommers empty, mixHash=0), state root, transaction execution. Fork choice state (head, safe, finalized hashes) must reference known valid blocks.

Full PoW validation: difficulty target verification, total difficulty computation against TTD, ethash proof verification. Blocks claiming to reach TTD must be carefully validated to prevent premature or malicious merge triggering.

ECDSA signature must be recovered and signer verified against authorized set. Signing frequency limit enforced (1 per floor(N/2)+1 blocks). Timestamp >= parent + BLOCK_PERIOD. ExtraData format validated. Checkpoint blocks require embedded signer list, nonce=0, beneficiary=0. Vote tallying for signer set changes requires majority threshold.
Contract must extract chain ID from signed message and compare against CHAINID opcode result. Mismatch indicates cross-chain replay attempt and must be rejected.

Builder BLS signature must be verified against registered builder_index. Builder must have sufficient excess balance for bid value. execution_payment must equal zero for gossip bids. parent_block_hash and parent_block_root must reference valid chain state. Slot must be current or next.

Envelope must match previously accepted bid (block_hash). Builder signature must be verified. State root must be correct (computed from process_execution_payload). Payload content must pass full EL validation.
Withdrawal credentials must have BUILDER_WITHDRAWAL_PREFIX (0x03). Address format must be validated. Deposit amount must meet minimum requirements.

Address parameter must be valid Ethereum format. ChainId, limit, and asset types must be validated. User consent must be obtained before returning asset data. Only whitelisted assets should be shared. dApp identity should be verified to prevent phishing.

Full blob transaction validation required: type-3 format, non-nil 'to' address, secp256k1 signature, min 1 blob, versioned hash prefix 0x01, sender balance coverage for execution + blob gas, max_fee_per_blob_gas >= blob base fee. For subscriptions: filter parameter validation (from/to address format, hasReturnData boolean).
Validate devp2p packet size (10MB limit), hash count limits (4096 for announcements, 256 for requests), transaction content matches announced hashes, blob sidecar KZG proof verification.

Fork ID is not cryptographically authenticated. Validation uses CRC32 comparison and subset/superset relationship checks. Malicious peers can lie about fork ID; this is a best-effort filter, not a security boundary.

JWT-authenticated channel, but CL must validate: execution request type ordering (ascending, no duplicates), per-payload request limits, deserialization correctness. Withdrawal root in payload must match hash_tree_root of expected withdrawals from get_expected_withdrawals. Parent hash, prev_randao, and timestamp consistency required.

Must verify: validator index exists, current withdrawal credentials use 0x00 BLS prefix, BLS pubkey hash matches credential bytes 1-31, BLS signature is valid using fork-agnostic DOMAIN_BLS_TO_EXECUTION_CHANGE. This is an irreversible one-way credential migration.

Must resolve fork-appropriate generalized indices (Altair vs Electra) based on attested slot epoch. Verify finalized root Merkle branch and sync committee Merkle branch using resolved gindices. Validate sync committee BLS aggregate signature. Fork-specific execution payload header hashing (Capella/Deneb/Electra) for backward compatibility.

Batch verify cell KZG proofs using Fiat-Shamir challenge derivation and BLS12-381 pairing check. Deduplicate commitments for efficiency. If batch verification fails, must perform individual cell verification to identify invalid proofs. Recovery requires at least 50% valid cells; corrupted cells must be excluded before recovery attempt.

Validate input exactly 192 bytes. Parse and validate versioned hash (0x01 prefix), z and y as BLS12-381 field elements (< BLS_MODULUS), 48-byte G1 commitments and proofs. Verify computed versioned hash matches input. Verify KZG proof via pairing check. Fixed 50,000 gas cost. All cryptographic exceptions caught and converted to KZGProofError.

Full transaction validation required: signature recovery (ECDSA), nonce check, gas limit validation, EIP-7623 calldata floor cost, intrinsic gas calculation, init code size limit (EIP-3860), transaction type decoding, and balance sufficiency check.
Must validate VersionedHash format, KZG commitment integrity, blob gas pricing, and all standard transaction validation. Blob count limits must be enforced.

Full block validation: header validity (parent hash, gas limits, base fee calculation), transaction list integrity, state root verification after applying all transactions, withdrawal processing, request aggregation (deposits, withdrawals, consolidations).

JWT authentication verified. Payload content must still be validated: execution payload structure, block hash consistency, state transition correctness. Paris merge constraints enforced (difficulty=0, nonce=0, empty ommers).
Validate proposer signature, slot assignment, attestation validity, slashing conditions. Reject duplicate or conflicting attestations.
Validate SSZ container structure per EIP-7688 ProgressiveContainer rules. Verify stable generalized indices, active field bitmask, and merkle proof consistency across fork transitions.
Proof verification must handle ProgressiveContainer generalized indices correctly. Edge cases in container migration (active fields vs inactive fields) must not produce invalid proofs.
Smart contract must receive valid proof data. Generalized indices must remain stable across forks per EIP-7688. Malformed proof inputs must not cause EVM execution anomalies.
Provider registration must validate provider object structure. SVG icon data must be sanitized to prevent XSS. Object.freeze must be applied to prevent provider list tampering.
User wallet selection must be validated. DApp must not be able to override user preference or inject fake providers.

Hardware wallet must correctly interpret EIP-7688 ProgressiveContainer format. Signed data must match expected container hash. Migration from one container version to another must not break signing compatibility.
All blocks and transactions received via P2P must be fully validated. Eclipse attack mitigations required. Peer reputation scoring should limit impact of malicious peers.
Block bids from relays must be validated for correctness. Relay-provided execution payloads must pass full EL validation before inclusion. Censorship resistance mechanisms should be considered.

All three validation checks must pass: (1) submitter is a member of the inclusion list committee for the specified slot, (2) inclusion_list_committee_root matches the Merkle root of the actual committee, (3) BLS signature is valid under DOMAIN_INCLUSION_LIST_COMMITTEE.

Block proposals must be validated for inclusion list compliance. Non-compliant blocks (missing forced transactions) must be deprioritized by fork choice. The union of all valid inclusion list transactions must be checked.

Full EOF container validation is required at deployment time: magic byte check, version validation, section order enforcement, type section size divisibility, code section minimum size, MAX_INITCODE_SIZE limit, and no stray bytes. Legacy bytecode must also undergo jump destination analysis.

All call data and target addresses are untrusted. Jump targets must be validated against pre-computed valid_jump_destinations set. EOF opcode restrictions must be enforced (reject list). DELEGATECALL from EOF to legacy must fail. Invalid opcodes must cause execution revert.

Full validation pipeline required: (1) slot matches current slot within MAXIMUM_GOSSIP_CLOCK_DISPARITY, (2) validator belongs to the sync committee subnet, (3) no duplicate message from this validator for this slot on this subnet, (4) BLS signature over beacon block root is valid.

Full contribution validation required: slot check, subcommittee_index bounds, aggregation_bits non-empty, aggregator selection proof validity, aggregator subcommittee membership, and both selection proof and aggregate BLS signatures verified.

Messages must be correctly identified via domain-separated SHA256 hashing. Valid Snappy decompression uses MESSAGE_DOMAIN_VALID_SNAPPY; failed decompression uses MESSAGE_DOMAIN_INVALID_SNAPPY. This separation prevents message ID collisions between valid and invalid messages.

Committee membership must be verified BEFORE caching to prevent gossip mutation attacks. The committee_bits field (unsigned, outside signed data) must be cross-checked against actual committee assignments. This prevents attackers from modifying the committee index during gossip propagation.

Full parameter validation required: (1) chainId is valid hex format, (2) rpcUrls non-empty with HTTPS scheme only, (3) no duplicate chain, (4) eth_chainId response from RPC matches submitted chainId, (5) nativeCurrency object valid if present, (6) explicit user consent with requester identification and RPC exposure warning. The submitted chainId (not RPC-reported) must be used for signing.

ENR records in NODES responses must be verified via their embedded signatures. Routing table updates must respect k-bucket limits (max 16 per bucket). Stale nodes must be evicted via liveness checks (PING). Response size limited to 16 result nodes per FINDNODE.

All incoming UDP packets must be: (1) header-unmasked using local node ID, (2) protocol ID and version verified, (3) message decrypted and authenticated via AES-GCM. Failed decryption triggers WHOAREYOU challenge for session establishment. Packet size must not exceed 1280 bytes.

All gossip messages must be decompressed (snappy), size-validated (<= 10 MiB), message-ID computed, and content-validated per topic-specific rules (signature, slot, committee). REJECT messages penalize peer score.
Oversized messages must be dropped and sender penalized via peer scoring. Snappy decompression must enforce size limit before full decompression to prevent memory exhaustion.
Message timestamps must be within 500ms tolerance. Messages from the future beyond this window must be IGNORED (not REJECTED) to avoid penalizing peers with slight clock drift.
Fork digest must be compared on connection. Mismatched fork digests require immediate disconnect. Status fields (finalized checkpoint, head) must not be blindly trusted for chain state decisions.

Block difficulty must be independently computed from parent header and compared against claimed difficulty. Difficulty bomb delay offset (9,000,000 for Muir Glacier) must be correctly applied. Invalid difficulty must cause block rejection.

Block number must be checked against fork activation threshold to select correct validation ruleset. All 9 Byzantium EIPs must activate atomically at the fork block. Blocks from non-upgraded peers on different rules must be rejected.

Block number used for difficulty calculation must be the canonical chain height. The bomb delay offset must be applied correctly (max(0, block_number - 9,000,000)). Integer underflow must be prevented via clamping to zero.

Inclusion lists must be received before view freeze deadline. Equivocation (conflicting lists from same validator for same slot/root) must be detected and the validator's lists excluded from aggregation. Transactions must be deduplicated.
Block builders must be constrained by separate enforcement mechanisms to actually include required transactions. The inclusion list store must correctly exclude equivocators from the transaction set.

Request must be validated: asset type recognized, address checksum verified, chain ID validated. Image URLs must be checked for dangerous schemes (file://, http://) and SSRF (localhost/internal targets). Token similarity must be checked against known token lists for phishing. Response must be returned before user interaction to prevent fingerprinting.

All SSZ deserialization must validate: offset ordering and range, no excess trailing bytes, list capacity limits, union selector bounds (0-127), bitlist sentinel presence. Malformed data must be rejected. Implementations should enforce maximum nesting depth to prevent stack overflow.

Raw SSZ bytes must be deserialized with full validation before use in consensus logic. Deserialization failures must not cause crashes or undefined behavior. Memory allocation during deserialization must be bounded by declared type limits.
Full transaction validation required: authorization list validation, chain ID check, nonce bounds, ECDSA signature recovery, existing code check, delegation target validation.
Request parsing and validation required. Response must reflect correct chain ID from head block configuration. No authentication required but rate limiting recommended.

Standard transaction validation. BASEFEE value is derived from block context (not user input) so the opcode itself is safe, but contracts using BASEFEE for pricing must handle manipulation by block producers.
