Input parsing must handle: short input (zero-padding), zero-length fields, extremely large length values, modulus=0 edge case, gas cost must scale with operand complexity to prevent DoS.
Full block header validation required: parent hash, state root, transactions root, receipts root, withdrawals root, requests hash (SHA2-256), blob gas fields. Malformed RLP must be rejected.

Withdrawal data (index, validator_index, address, amount) comes from CL via authenticated Engine API. Content validation required: sequential indices, valid addresses, correct Gwei amounts. Withdrawals root must match header commitment.
Requests hash in header must be recomputed from block execution results and verified against the SHA2-256 commitment. CL provides the header but EL independently validates.

Payload and blobs_bundle from EL must be validated: KZG commitments must match blob data, blob count within MAX_BLOB_COMMITMENTS_PER_BLOCK, execution_payload must be consistent with PayloadAttributes sent.
Full sidecar validation required: blob index within bounds, KZG proof against commitment, Merkle inclusion proof linking commitment to block body, signed block header verification.
Serve only validated sidecars within retention window. Rate limit sync requests to prevent resource exhaustion.

Full bid validation: BLS signature verification, builder active status in registry (verified via finalized checkpoint), balance >= bid_value + MIN_DEPOSIT_AMOUNT + pending_withdrawals, matching slot/parent_block_hash/randao, blob commitment count within limits, parent block fullness check.
Payload envelope must match accepted bid: builder signature, payload consistency with bid commitments, blob data matching KZG commitments. PTC attestation determines builder payment.

No authentication possible for browser extensions. DApps must: freeze provider detail objects (Object.freeze), render SVG icons only via tag to prevent script execution, detect duplicate UUIDs as impersonation attempts, treat rdns as advisory only.

Full validation pipeline: JSON parse, RPC structure check, method lookup, parameter validation (0x-prefix, Quantity/Data encoding), hex decode, RLP decode, ECDSA signature verification, nonce/balance checks, fee structure validation (maxFee >= baseFee, priority <= maxFee), blob-specific checks (EIP-4844), init code size limits, authorization list validation (EIP-7702).

Message type validation required: reject deprecated GetNodeData (0x0d) and NodeData (0x0e). Valid messages require full content validation (block headers, transactions). Snap protocol (GetByteCodes, GetTrieNodes) messages require separate validation.
Full block header validation, transaction validation including SELFDESTRUCT behavior (EIP-6780: same-TX creation check), excess_blob_gas verification with EIP-7918 reserve price conditional logic.

No built-in authentication. Security depends entirely on infrastructure-level protections (reverse proxy, firewall). Heavy endpoints (state queries, validator duties) are DoS vectors. Rate limiting recommended. Must not be exposed to public internet without security layers.

Proof engine output crosses a trust boundary. Prover must validate proof content before signing with BLS. Domain separation via DOMAIN_EXECUTION_PROOF prevents cross-domain replay. Invalid proofs from a compromised engine could deceive stateless validators if signed by a whitelisted prover.

Full validation pipeline: non-empty proof data check, proof engine cryptographic verification, duplicate detection by request root + proof type, BLS signature verification against whitelisted prover public key with DOMAIN_EXECUTION_PROOF.

Engine API is JWT-authenticated. Fork choice updates must be processed atomically. Finalized payloads must be irreversibly persisted. Re-org protection via should_override_forkchoice_update requires all 8 conditions to be simultaneously true.

Terminal PoW block must satisfy: total_difficulty >= TERMINAL_TOTAL_DIFFICULTY AND parent_total_difficulty < TERMINAL_TOTAL_DIFFICULTY. Or if TERMINAL_BLOCK_HASH is set, exact hash match required at correct epoch. Unavailable PoW data must trigger graceful degradation (deferred processing), not block rejection.

Validators must independently recalculate excess_blob_gas using the modified formula with reserve price conditional logic. Header value must match recalculated value exactly. Both reserve mode (BLOB_BASE_COST * base_fee > GAS_PER_BLOB * blob_base_fee) and normal mode formulas must be correctly implemented.
Method must not leak sensitive internal information. Rate limiting recommended to prevent enumeration abuse.
All RPC method calls must be validated. Reserved rpc.* namespace must be enforced.
Provider must validate RequestArguments. Sensitive methods must require user authorization (error 4100). Request/response translation must not introduce injection.
Nonce must be verified for freshness/replay protection. Path permissions must be validated. User consent must be obtained before granting permissions.

All length fields and operands must be parsed safely with zero-padding for short inputs. Gas cost must accurately reflect computational complexity to prevent DoS. Modulus-zero edge case must return zero.
Input points must be validated on curve. Coordinates must be checked against field modulus. Invalid inputs must raise OutOfGasError.
G1 point must be validated on curve. Scalar input is arbitrary 256-bit value. Gas cost (6000) must accurately reflect worst-case computation.

Input length must be divisible by 192. All G1/G2 points must be validated on curve AND in correct prime-order subgroup. Gas cost is linear in pair count. Subgroup check is critical for pairing security.

Receipt count must match transaction count. Individual receipt size bounded by gas_limit/8. Total size bounded by block gas limit. Peer must be penalized for invalid data. Buffer sizes must be bounded to prevent memory exhaustion.
Request parameters must be validated. Response size must be bounded. firstBlockReceiptIndex must be within valid range.
DApp must verify provider identity. Multiple provider conflicts must be handled. Injected provider must not be modifiable by page scripts.
User must be shown clear, accurate information about what they are approving. Phishing-resistant UI required.
Provider should validate response format. Connection should be over secure transport. Timeouts must be implemented.

ALL signing requests MUST be checked against persistent slashing protection DB BEFORE signing. Block proposals must not duplicate slots. Attestations must not create double/surround votes. Far-future attestation check required (~6 hours threshold).
Committee assignments and chain state from beacon node must be used carefully. Validator should cross-check critical data where possible.
All received attestations must be fully validated (signature, committee membership, slot timing). Invalid attestations must be rejected.
Aggregate proofs must verify selection proof, aggregator index, and aggregate signature. Must be rate-limited.
Deposits must include valid Merkle proofs. ETH1 block candidates must satisfy follow distance and timestamp range. ETH1 endpoint could be compromised.

Full nodes must serve data with valid Merkle proofs. Light clients must verify sync committee signatures and proofs. Updates must be ranked by is_better_update. Data withholding cannot be detected cryptographically.
Genesis data integrity must be verified (e.g., hash comparison). No authentication specified; HTTPS assumed but not guaranteed.
Single bootnode is a centralization/availability risk. Peer list from bootnode must not be blindly trusted. Eclipse attack mitigation needed.
Stats data should not leak sensitive node information. Connection should be optional and authenticated.
Experimental opcodes (EIP-2315 subroutines, EIP-2537 BLS) must be fully validated. Standard transaction validation applies.
Configuration inputs should be validated. Genesis file integrity should be verified against known hash.

Full transaction validation required: signature s-value <= secp256k1n/2 (EIP-2), nonce < 2^64-1 (EIP-2681), gas limit <= 2^63-1 (EIP-7675/EIP-4803), sender is EOA not contract (EIP-3607/EIP-7675), valid transaction encoding. All calldata bytes contribute to gas cost at 15/60 gas per zero/non-zero byte (EIP-8007/EIP-7976).

Transaction parameters (from, to, gas, gasPrice) must be validated. Method must be eth_sendTransaction (eth_sign prohibited). Read-only iframe requests filtered against 43-method whitelist. Browser same-origin policy assumed to enforce domain isolation.
RPC method must be in allowedMethods whitelist. JSON-RPC request must be parseable. Methods requiring account unlock are rejected.
User approval triggers 3-second account unlock window. Authorization popup must accurately display transaction details. UI spoofing must be prevented by the browser environment.

Blocks must be validated against fork-specific consensus rules. For Muir Glacier (EIP-2387): verify block number >= 9,200,000 triggers EIP-2384 difficulty bomb delay. Difficulty calculation must use correct fake block number offset. All transactions in block must pass all validation rules.

All precompile inputs arrive via transactions from untrusted users. ALT_BN128: validate input length (64/128/192*n bytes), field element < modulus, point on curve, subgroup membership. BLS12-381: validate input length per operation type, field elements < BLS12 modulus, point on curve, subgroup check (point * curve_order == infinity). BLAKE2F: validate input exactly 213 bytes, final flag in {0,1}. Gas must be correctly charged before execution.

All system opcode invocations originate from user transactions. Must validate: init code size <= MAX_INIT_CODE_SIZE, address collision checks (EIP-7610 storage collision), call depth <= 1024, sender nonce < 2^64-1, sender balance >= endowment/value, static context restrictions for value transfer and SELFDESTRUCT. EIP-6780: SELFDESTRUCT only deletes contracts created in same transaction.

EXTCODEADDRESS resolves only one level of delegation. Delegation target is NOT warmed (subsequent cold access costs apply). Sponsorship contracts must verify delegation target against whitelist. Delegation can change between transactions (TOCTOU risk).
JWT authentication validates channel but payload content must be validated. Block payloads must pass all EL validation rules. The CL is trusted for fork choice but not for payload correctness.

CL must independently validate all request contents. requests_hash (SHA256) in block header provides integrity commitment. Requests sorted by type ascending; empty requests excluded from hash. CL rejection does not affect EL block validity. Each request type has its own validation rules defined by subsequent EIPs.
Full transaction validation required: EIP-1559 fee fields (max_fee_per_gas >= base_fee), balance check (gas_limit * max_fee + value), EIP-155 chain ID verification, signature recovery, nonce check.
Query parameters must be validated. Bloom filter pre-filtering reduces I/O but false positives require full log verification. Rate limiting recommended to prevent resource exhaustion.
ABI-to-data function selector validation is mandatory. Selector match does NOT guarantee ABI accuracy (4-byte collision possible). Wallet must clearly indicate ABI source is untrusted DApp.
EIP-155 chain ID must be extracted from v parameter and verified against network CHAIN_ID. Legacy v=27/28 transactions accepted for backward compatibility but lack cross-chain replay protection.

All P2P-received transactions require identical validation as RPC-submitted transactions. Additionally, replay attack detection via EIP-155 chain ID check. Transactions with mismatched chain IDs must be rejected.

Block validation must verify: EIP-1559 base fee matches calculation from parent, gas limit within ±1/1024 of parent, gas_used <= gas_limit, minimum gas limit >= 5000, all receipt status codes (EIP-658) correctly reflect execution outcomes.

JWT authentication validates channel identity. EL must independently validate all payload content: block structure, state transitions, receipt generation. Safe block hash from CL (justified checkpoint) must be used only as advisory — EL should not assume safe block is finalized.
JWT authentication validates channel identity. CL must handle invalid/syncing responses gracefully. Incorrect VALID status for an invalid payload could cause CL to build on an invalid chain.

Fork digest verification required at connection time. During fork transitions (Fulu, EIP-6800, EIP-7892 BPO forks), peers with mismatched fork digests must be disconnected. ENR nfd field must be validated. All gossip messages require full consensus validation regardless of peer identity.

Light client requests must be rate-limited. Deneb-format headers must include blob_gas_used and excess_blob_gas only for blocks at or after DENEB_FORK_EPOCH. Pre-Deneb blocks must use legacy header format.

Must validate transaction type byte (0-0x7f range), reject unknown types with peer disconnect (SHOULD), validate payload per type-specific rules. Must not process transactions for types not yet activated by fork block.

Full block validation required: header validation (gas, difficulty, PoW), ommer validation (max 2, age 1-6), transaction list validation (all types known and valid), state/receipt/tx root verification. Reject blocks with unknown transaction types.

Full transaction validation: signature recovery, nonce match, balance >= gas*price + value, sender is EOA, gas available in block. For access list txs: validate access list entries. For blob txs: validate blob gas pricing (GAS_PER_BLOB * count * blob_base_fee).

PoW validation (Ethash, mix digest, difficulty target), extraData validation during DAO fork range (blocks 1920000-1920009 must contain 'dao-hard-fork'), difficulty calculation with bomb delay. All state roots must be recomputed and verified.

Gas metering must accurately reflect computation cost. Identity: base + per-word. SHA256: base + per-word. Arbitrary input size bounded only by gas. No content validation needed (precompiles are pure functions).
Must verify caller's DAO token balance via mainDAO contract before transferring proportional ether. Transfer failure must throw exception.

JWT authentication verified. Execution payload content must still be validated: state transition correctness, gas accounting, transaction execution. EIP-8025 dual validation requires both ExecutionEngine and ProofEngine agreement.

Must validate committee_bits (within MAX_COMMITTEES_PER_SLOT), compute attesting indices from aggregation_bits, verify aggregate BLS signature. Detect conflicting attestations for slashing (penalty: effective_balance / 4096).

Validate BLS deposit signature (is_valid_deposit_signature). Queue as PendingDeposit. Process at epoch boundary respecting: finality check (deposit slot must be finalized), MAX_PENDING_DEPOSITS_PER_EPOCH (16), activation churn limits. EL enforces MAX_DEPOSIT_REQUESTS_PER_PAYLOAD (8192).

Validate source_address matches 0x01 withdrawal credentials, validator is active and not exiting. Amount=0 means full exit (compute exit epoch with churn). Non-zero amount queues PendingPartialWithdrawal. Max 16 per payload. Sweep max 8 per block.

Validate source_address matches withdrawal credentials, both validators active, source != target, neither slashed. Same-validator triggers compounding switch (0x01 -> 0x02). Cross-validator queues PendingConsolidation. Max 2 per payload.

Three-stage validation: (1) prover_pubkey belongs to active validator, (2) BLS signature valid under DOMAIN_EXECUTION_PROOF, (3) proof cryptographically valid via proof_engine.verify_execution_proof. Reject at any failure stage. Max proof size 300 KiB.

Proof generation must use stable generalized indices that are capacity-independent. Progressive tree structure must provide equivalent security to fixed-capacity merkle trees. Context-specific bounds enforcement required.

Recipient public key should be verified via signerPubKey signature and optional trustedPubKey chain. Ephemeral keys must use CSRNG. ECDH shared secret derived correctly. AES-GCM encryption with HKDF-derived key/IV. Ephemeral keys must be securely destroyed after protocol completion for PFS.

Full block header and body validation required: block number, timestamp, gas limit, gas used, extra data, parent hash, difficulty (pre-merge), PoW (pre-merge). All data from peers is potentially malicious.
Requests must be bounded by HISTORY_PRUNE_EPOCHS window. Resource exhaustion prevention required for serving peers.

Full transaction validation required: intrinsic gas, sender recovery, nonce check, balance check. All calldata is potentially malicious including calls to precompiles (P-256, ECDSA) and system contracts (EIP-2935 history, EIP-7002 withdrawals).

EL validates: input format (exactly 56 bytes), fee payment (msg.value >= current_fee). CL validates: source_address matches validator's withdrawal credentials. Dynamic fee mechanism must resist spam attacks.
Checkpoint must be validated against known chain state. Must be within weak subjectivity period. Invalid checkpoint enables long-range attacks and syncing to invalid chain.
All historical data must be verified against known state roots or accumulator proofs. Data integrity cannot be assumed from the transport channel.

API access must be restricted to authorized proof engines. Proof content must be cryptographically verified via verify_execution_proof(). Proof type must match requested ProofAttributes. Timeout handling required for missing/delayed proofs.
Block difficulty must be independently recalculated using correct formula (including EIP-5133 bomb delay offset). Stated difficulty must match computed expected difficulty exactly.

Full schema validation required: non-empty container, max 256 fields, no trailing zeros in active_fields, field count matches active bits. Deserialized containers must have absent fields defaulted to zero. Merkle root must include active_fields mix-in.

Full proof path verification required. active_fields mix-in must be verified to prevent collision between absent fields and zero values. Gindex stability ensures backward compatibility but proofs from untrusted sources must be fully validated.

All sync committee messages must be validated: (1) sender is in current sync committee, (2) signature is valid over the correct beacon block root, (3) message timing is within acceptable window per SYNC_MESSAGE_DUE_BPS.

Aggregated contributions must be validated: (1) aggregation bits and signatures are consistent, (2) included individual messages are valid, (3) submission timing is within CONTRIBUTION_DUE_BPS window.

Full validation required: (1) source address is 20 bytes, source/target pubkeys are 48 bytes each, (2) fee payment covers computed exponential fee, (3) queue has not exceeded 262,144 capacity limit. Requests exceeding capacity are discarded without refund.

Exit requests must be validated against validator registry. Weight-based churn limiting (256 ETH initial limit) must correctly handle partial exits and deferred processing. Large validator exits (up to 2048 ETH) must not bypass churn limits.

Full transaction validation pipeline: (1) type detection via first byte ([0x00-0x7f] typed, [0xc0-0xfe] legacy), (2) type-specific payload decoding and validation, (3) signature verification with type byte in signed data (domain separation), (4) fee validation (max_fee >= base_fee, priority_fee <= max_fee), (5) nonce and balance checks.

Blob-specific validation required: (1) blob gas within protocol limit, (2) max_fee_per_blob_gas >= current blob base fee, (3) versioned hash has correct 0x01 prefix and 32-byte length with valid KZG correspondence, (4) blob data actually present, (5) contract creation prohibited for Type 3.

Auth packet must be decryptable via ECIES with recipient's static key. Required fields (signature, initiator-pubk, initiator-nonce) must be present. Version mismatches and extra RLP elements are tolerated per EIP-8 but must not cause crashes or buffer overflows. Random padding (100-300 bytes) should use cryptographically secure randomness.

Hello packets parsed with forward-compatible tolerance. Version mismatches ignored. Capability advertisements must not be trusted without further protocol-level validation. Additional list elements and trailing data ignored safely.

Packets must not exceed 1280 bytes. Unknown packet types silently discarded. Known types (ping/pong/findnode/neighbours) processed with tolerant RLP parsing. UDP source addresses are spoofable — no authentication at transport level.

Permission system must: (1) correctly identify invoker origin without spoofing, (2) present clear consent UI resistant to clickjacking, (3) enforce caveat restrictions on method calls, (4) validate URLs against SSRF (scheme and port whitelisting), (5) filter permissions by invoker on query. Error 4001 returned on user rejection per EIP-1193.

Signed data MUST include TransactionType byte as first byte to ensure domain separation per EIP-2718. Signature verification must reject signatures where type byte is missing or mismatched, preventing cross-type signature reuse attacks.

Conversion must correctly map gas_price to both max_fee_per_gas and max_priority_fee_per_gas. Access list must be preserved unchanged. Chain ID must be maintained. Type field updated from 0x1 to 0x2. Incorrect conversion could alter transaction economics.

All light client updates must be cryptographically verified: BLS aggregate signature verification over sync committee, Merkle branch verification for finality and execution payload proofs, slot ordering validation, and minimum participation threshold checks.

Full cryptographic verification pipeline required: sync committee signature verification, finality Merkle proof verification, execution payload Merkle proof verification (Capella+). No update should be applied without passing all validation steps.

The trusted block root MUST correspond to a canonical chain block. If this root is compromised, all subsequent light client validation is compromised. This is the root of trust for the entire light client protocol. Users must obtain this via reliable out-of-band channels.

JWT authentication validates the channel. However, execution payload content must be fully validated: parent hash consistency, RANDAO mix, timestamp alignment, blob commitment counts, transaction validity, and (post-EIP-6800) Verkle witness verification. The CL relays proposer data which may be adversarial.

Block proposer data must be validated through complete consensus validation pipeline: slot verification, proposer eligibility, execution payload validity via Engine API, and (post-EIP-6800) Verkle witness structural and cryptographic verification.

The CL trusts the EL to correctly verify execution payloads and return accurate results. JWT authenticates the channel. The CL cannot independently re-verify execution-layer state transitions. A compromised EL would compromise CL's view of execution validity.

All blocks and transactions from P2P peers must be independently validated: block header fields (difficulty, gas limit, timestamp), transaction signatures, nonce ordering, gas pricing, state transition correctness. Eclipse attack mitigations required.

Block difficulty must be independently recalculated using the difficulty formula with fork-adjusted block numbers (post-Muir Glacier: max(0, block.number - 9,000,000)). Stated difficulty in headers cannot be trusted.

Full transaction validation required: signature verification, nonce validation, gas limit checks, balance sufficiency (or zero-balance handling per EIP-7768), contract code size limits (24KB per EIP-170), and state clearing rules (EIP-161). For EIP-7768 no-ether transactions, proposer must perform double-execution verification to ensure consideration consistency.

Column sidecar data must be verified against KZG commitments from the beacon block. Peers may serve invalid columns or withhold data. Custody group assignments must be independently computed. ENR custody claims cannot be trusted without verification.

All validator messages must be validated against consensus rules. Invalid blocks must be rejected. Conflicting attestations must trigger slashing detection. Proposer eligibility must be verified. No validator message should be trusted based solely on validator identity.

Execution payloads from external builders via MEV-Boost relays must be fully validated through the same pipeline as locally-built payloads. No trust should be placed in relay assertions about payload validity or value. Relay availability cannot be guaranteed.
Block must pass signature verification, slot validation, parent existence check, and state transition validation before being accepted into fork choice. Equivocating proposers must be detected.

PTC attestations must verify: validator is in assigned PTC committee for the slot, attestation signature is valid, and validator index maps correctly to ptc_vote boolean vector. Quorum threshold (>256/512) required before payload timeliness is accepted.

Execution payload envelope must be verified for data availability (blob KZG commitments). JWT authentication validates the channel but payload content integrity must be checked independently. Payload must correspond to a known block.

Full transaction validation required: signature verification, nonce check, gas limit validation, init code execution, and returned bytecode size check (<=24576 bytes per EIP-170). Out-of-gas on size violation.
Blocks from P2P must be fully validated: header verification, transaction execution, state root comparison, contract size limits enforcement. Size-bounded verification time guaranteed by EIP-170.

All RPC inputs must be validated: address format, storage key format, block identifier resolution, parameter bounds. Rate limiting and request size limits should prevent DoS. Storage key count for eth_getProof should be bounded.

Proof data from untrusted RPC providers must be cryptographically verified against a trusted stateRoot. Each node in accountProof and storageProof must be hashed and path-validated. Non-existence proofs must show divergence or empty branch.

JWT authentication required on the channel. Payload content must be fully validated: transaction execution, state root computation, gas accounting, receipt verification. The EL must not trust CL-provided execution data without independent verification.

Input must be validated: length divisible by 192, G1 coordinates < p and on curve (or zero point), G2 coordinates valid in F_p² with correct subgroup order q. Gas cost (80000*k + 100000) must be pre-deducted. Invalid input must revert consuming all gas.

Block headers are trusted based on consensus mechanism (PoS finality). The stateRoot in the header serves as the cryptographic trust anchor. Light client sync protocol must verify committee signatures and finality checkpoints.
EL must independently validate fork activation criteria (block number/timestamp). JWT authentication ensures channel integrity but fork parameters must be verified against local configuration.
Full transaction validation required: signature verification, nonce check, gas limit validation, balance sufficiency, EIP-2718 type envelope parsing.
Input parameters must be validated to prevent resource exhaustion during estimation. Malformed transaction parameters should be rejected before simulation.
Full block validation required: header validation, transaction execution, state root verification, receipt root verification. Malformed blocks must be rejected without crashing.

Deposit logs must be filtered by exact contract address (0x00000000219ab540356cbb839cbe05303d7705fa) and event signature hash. Data must be exactly 576 bytes. Field parsing is structural; cryptographic validation deferred to CL.

Economic cost of deposit spam (~1000 ETH per second of delay) provides primary defense. Maximum 8192 deposits per payload caps worst-case processing. BLS signature verification timing must be bounded.

Index reuse must atomically clear equivocation history via on_reused_index(). Attacker must not be able to time deposits to receive specific indices. is_reusable_validator() must enforce sufficient cooldown period.
Fork version must be validated before SSZ deserialization. Light client updates must be verified against sync committee signatures. Rate limiting via gossipsub scoring assumed.
Bootstrap data must be validated against known checkpoint. Fork-versioned SSZ type must match expected fork version for the requested slot. Malformed responses must be rejected.

Fork version must be determined from slot/epoch before selecting SSZ type. Deserialization with wrong type must fail safely without crashes or memory corruption. Messages at genesis fork version must be rejected.

Checkpoint root and epoch must be validated against chain state. Node must verify it is within the weak subjectivity period. If outside WS period, node must halt and require operator intervention for fresh checkpoint.
Conflicting chains must be rejected if they disagree with a valid WS checkpoint within the WS period. Node must track WS period expiry and refuse to sync if exceeded.

Effective balances must be frozen at epoch N - MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD - 1 before RANDAO for epoch N is known. Proposer schedule stored in state must be immutable once computed. Lookahead vector must be initialized correctly at fork activation.

RANDAO values must be unpredictable at the time effective balances are set. MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD provides the temporal separation. If RANDAO prediction advances, the security margin must be re-evaluated.

All public keys must pass KeyValidate before aggregation. Empty pubkey sets must only accept G2 point at infinity as valid signature. FastAggregateVerify must be used for non-empty sets. BLS library must conform to IETF draft v4.

Index reuse requires: (1) current_epoch > withdrawable_epoch + SAFE_EPOCHS_TO_REUSE_INDEX (65536), (2) balance == 0. Iteration order must be deterministic (ascending index). Overwriting validator record must clear all equivocation history.

External systems must be aware that validator index identity can change after reuse. APIs should expose pubkey changes. The 0.8-year time-lock is assumed sufficient for all historical references to become stale.

Gas cost must accurately reflect computation: minimum floor of 500 gas, multiplication complexity based on operand size with minimum 32-byte assumption, iteration count with 16x multiplier for large exponents. Malformed inputs must fail with all gas consumed.

Shuffle proof must validate 124-tracker permutation via Curdleproofs ZK scheme. Opening proof must verify knowledge of secret k. k_commitment must be unique across all validators. First-time registration must verify tracker.r_G != BLS_G1_GENERATOR. All proof failures must cause block rejection.

RLP structure must be validated: [request_id, [payload]] format with valid 64-bit request_id. Response correlation must handle duplicate IDs safely. Pending request tracking must have timeouts to prevent memory exhaustion from request flooding.

Pre-Capella data must be validated before local conversion. Empty ExecutionPayloadHeader and ExecutionBranch defaults used during upgrade must not pass validation as real execution data. Upgrade functions should guard against double-application.
